Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
On the Run
Cardtype: Reaction
Disciplines: Celerity/Obfuscate
Only usable during a bleed action against you. Not usable by a blocking minion.
[cel][obf] Tap this vampire. You do not burn more than 2 pool during this action, regardless of the amount of the bleed.
[CEL][OBF] Tap this vampire. This turn, while this vampire is ready, you do not burn more than 2 pool during bleed actions against you, regardless of the amount of the bleed, and if this vampire is burned or goes to torpor, burn 3 pool.

Art notes: a hairy vampire in a suit, his tie untied, is fleeing at high speed in a dirty back alley, putting weight with one hand on a bin to jump over it, the other holding an attaché. Some running silhouettes in the shadow far behind are chasing him. The scene happens at night.

Prince of Paris, France

Messages.Author: extrala
Messages.Body:
I am not quite sure of if the superior effect is too strong, I was considering this in context of an Unnamed or IC bleed deck. You get a comparable effect (but transient) similar to Protected Resources, but without the drawback of not being able to bleed yourself.

Maybe instead of the torpor/burn clause, restrict the bleeds of the vampire (or of all of your vampires?) to 1 or 2 pool max. in your turn.

> On the Run
> Cardtype: Reaction
> Disciplines: Celerity/Obfuscate
> Only usable during a bleed action against you. Not usable by a blocking minion.
> [cel][obf] Tap this vampire. Reduce this bleed to a maximum of 2. This vampire cannot bleed for more than 2 during your next turn.
> [CEL][OBF] Tap this vampire. Reduce all bleeds during this turn to a maximum of 2. All of your vampires cannot bleed for more than 2 during your next turn.
>

Messages.Author: ReverendRevolver
Messages.Body:
Im not convinced thematically this card fits. Obf and Qui maybe, and thats because its hard to get at who assamites work for. But being hidden and fast making someone unable to bleed you for more than 2? Not feeling it. I mean, it addresses a problem assamites and city gangrel have, but id sooner see a bleed reduction reaction and a +2 stealth on an undirected action if a younger vamp is blocking at superior.

The super reducing at superior is just kinda crazy, and only falls when combat decks that bleed are yoir predator. Maybe Mattata gets a tier of souls and bleeds with deep song, or even plays Abo bleed pump, but otherwise, the drawback wont be worth playing it if yoi can be torped. Im not having Luke Fellows block Cock Robin. Heck, hes only gonna bleed for 2-3 normally, although cog+deepsong+tierofsouls with old friends migjt happen, its unlikely. You wouldnt play it agaimst most decks that rush because they will bleed for 2, then rush the guy, make you lose pool along with likely tension, them bleed more. Im thinking of germain or typical BnB builds, like pre pot, dom pot, or even what i use, dem pot.

Doesnt feel like a rrlevant drawback.

But the inf seems ok, even if i feel its off thematically.

For Nec needs bleed reduction more than obf cel, because nec can do it thematically, for has it already in vtes(just sucks) and samedi and harbingers(to a lesser degree) could use it/cooler stuff.

Messages.Author: kombainas
Messages.Body:
At least for Confusion of The Eye, the idea is that obfuscate allows you to trick someone you are someone else. So, playing, with the bleed is ok. Even more, it could be thematically as powerful as reduce bleed to 0 (by turning minion into someone familiar for the bleeder) or bouncing the bleed (by turning into the bleeding minion superior and giving new orders). However, obfuscate is strong as it is, and hardly needs another powercard.

However, celerity does not add ANYTHING to the thematic mix of countering bleeds. Perhaps just making a clan card would be thematically easier and would serve the need as well.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
The logic is simple:
It is harder to hit a moving target/resource.
It should be harder to hit one with vampiric speed...

The minion is effectively bundling up important resources and running away with them. Literally.

Story-type explanation
Fatima looks out the window to see what looks like shadows taking form, grabs her pack and any other valuables she can and sprints out moving between the shadows to make her escape.

Retired Baron of Sydney, Australia, 418
